page: Why Vite: addresses web development tooling pain points—slow dev server startup, sluggish hot updates, long production builds. Rethinks code serving during development vs incremental tool improvements. Evolved through multiple major versions adapting to ecosystem capabilities: native ES modules in browser, Rust-powered toolchain. Powers many frameworks/tools. Architecture evolves with web platform rather than locking into single approach. Long-term foundation for building. Origins: addressed bundle-based dev server slowness via ESM-based on-demand serving. Dependencies pre-bundled (fast), source code served on ESM demand (fast startup/HMR). Snowpack pioneered unbundled development + dependency pre-bundling concept. WMR inspired universal plugin API. @web/dev-server influenced Vite 1.0 server architecture. Ecosystem adoption: Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, React Router, Analog, SolidStart use Vite foundation. Vitest, Storybook built on Vite. Backend frameworks (Laravel, Rails) integrated Vite. Rolldown unification: Unified single bundler (was esbuild dev + Rollup build), Rust-powered, Oxc parsing/transforming/minifying, consistent pipeline dev-to-production. Future direction: full bundle mode exploration (reducing network overhead for large codebases), Environment API (custom environments beyond client/SSR), JavaScript evolution with Oxc/Rolldown collaboration.

sections.manifest: Origins of Vite: ES modules browser support enabled different approach. Traditional bundlers processed entire application upfront. Larger apps meant longer waits. Vite split work: Dependencies (pre-bundled once, fast native tooling, ready instantly). Source code (served on-demand over native ESM, transforms per-request). Dev server startup nearly instant regardless of app size. HMR via native ESM updated single module in browser without full reload. Bundle-based vs ESM-based comparison shown. Not first unbundled development tool: Snowpack pioneered unbundled + pre-bundling. WMR inspired universal plugin API (dev+build). @web/dev-server influenced Vite 1.0 architecture. Unbundled ESM inefficient for production (extra network round trips), bundling still necessary for optimized builds. Why bundlers necessary documentation.

Growing ecosystem: frameworks adopted Vite as build layer. Plugin API based on Rollup conventions enabled natural integration without workarounds. Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, React Router, Analog, SolidStart chose Vite foundation. Tools like Vitest (testing), Storybook (development environment) built on Vite, extended reach beyond app bundling. Backend frameworks integrated: Laravel Vite plugin, Ruby on Rails (vite-ruby). Growth bidirectional: Vite team runs vite-ecosystem-ci testing major projects on every change. Ecosystem CI part of release process. Ecosystem health prioritized. Testing major ecosystem projects catches regressions early.

Unified toolchain via Rolldown: Originally two separate tools—esbuild (dev fast compilation), Rollup (production optimization). Maintained two pipelines: inconsistencies in transformation, separate plugin systems, growing glue code. Rolldown built to unify: Rust-powered, native speed, Rollup plugin API compatibility (ecosystem relied on). Oxc used for parsing, transforming, minifying. End-to-end toolchain: build tool, bundler, compiler maintained together, evolve as unit. Result: consistent pipeline dev to production. Careful migration: technical preview shipped for early validation, ecosystem CI caught compatibility issues, compatibility layer preserved existing configurations.

Vite future direction: architecture continues evolving. Full bundle mode: unbundled ESM right tradeoff when created (no tool fast + HMR + plugins). Rolldown changes calculus. Exceptionally large codebases experience slow page loads (many unbundled requests). Team exploring bundled code mode during dev, reducing network overhead. Environment API: instead of client/SSR only build targets, frameworks define custom environments (edge runtimes, service workers, deployment targets). Each with own module resolution, execution rules. Where/how code runs diversifying, Vite model expands. JavaScript evolution: Oxc + Rolldown closely collaborate Vite, new language features/standards adopted quickly, entire toolchain, no upstream dependency waiting. Vite goal: not final tool, evolves with web platform and developers building on it.
